# Should We Invest in Solar?

Three solar proposals. One investment decision. Use Excel to build the evidence, test the assumptions and advise management.

:::

:::::: {.case-study aria-label="Cape Manufacturing case study: The investment brief"}
::: case-study-label
Case study · Cape Manufacturing · The investment brief
:::

Cape Manufacturing is a fictional Western Cape industrial producer facing material electricity costs. Three suppliers have proposed rooftop solar systems costing R650,000 to R990,000. Management wants to reduce grid purchases; any resilience benefit still needs verification. You have been employed as a trainee accountant to assist with the commercial analysis. The financial director has texted you with the following request:

::::: case-message
::: {.case-avatar aria-hidden="true"}
FD
:::

:::: case-message-body
::: case-meta
Monday 08:30 · Financial Director
:::

## Help us decide which solar proposal to take forward.

Welcome as our new trainee accountant. Please could you assist. You need to compare the proposals on a common basis, test the assumptions and bring me a recommendation this afternoon. We need evidence before committing capital.

## What you will learn

On successful completion of this activity, you should be able to:

1. Build an auditable Excel model comparing alternative investments.
2. Analyse financial results using payback, NPV and sensitivity analysis.
3. Evaluate assumptions and supplier claims using professional judgement and scepticism.
4. Communicate a concise, evidence-based recommendation to management.

## What you will produce

Your workbook will contain a Year-1 comparison, one management chart with a short design rationale, a sensitivity table and a recommendation of **100 words or fewer**. You will also request evidence for Supplier C’s environmental claim and briefly reflect on how your judgement developed.

The spreadsheet gives evidence. It does not choose the decision rule.

## Begin with the business problem

Open **Start Here** and read the brief. The five tabs keep the work traceable: **Start Here** provides orientation, **Case Data** holds inputs, **Your Model** contains your Year-1 calculations, **Test Assumptions** supports sensitivity analysis, and **Recommendation** records your advice.

Follow **Understand → Spreadsheet Essentials → Build → Test → Decide → Reflect**. Start by interpreting the supplier data before entering formulas. Spreadsheet Essentials provides the few prerequisite moves a beginner needs; later checkpoints help you diagnose errors as you work.

**For reviewers:** the [Reviewer Rationale](reviewer-rationale.qmd) provides a five-minute route through the Excel tasks, learning design and evidence of achievement.

:::: sa-context
::: label
South African commercial context
:::

Cape Manufacturing is a fictional Western Cape industrial producer. All monetary values are in South African Rand (R). The electricity tariff, escalation rate and other financial parameters are **assumptions**, not forecasts of South African tariffs or investment conditions. Unless stated otherwise, use the figures exactly as provided and do not introduce VAT, tax, financing or feed-in revenue into the model.

<details class="glossary-card">
<summary>Glossary &amp; further reading <span class="glossary-hint">· optional</span></summary>

Auditable model
:   A model whose inputs, formulas and results can be traced and checked by another person. It does not mean the workbook has undergone a formal audit.

Professional judgement
:   Applying relevant knowledge and weighing evidence, uncertainty and business priorities to reach a reasoned conclusion.

Professional scepticism
:   A questioning approach that critically assesses evidence and notices gaps or inconsistencies. It does not mean automatically distrusting a supplier.

Simple payback period
:   An estimate of how long savings take to recover the initial cost. This course uses installed cost divided by net Year-1 saving, without discounting future savings.

Net present value (NPV)
:   The value today of expected future net cash flows, less the initial investment. It helps compare long-term financial value under the chosen assumptions.

Sensitivity analysis
:   Testing how a model result changes when an assumption changes. Here, you explore whether lower use of System C’s solar output changes the preferred proposal.
